title: React Elements
definition: A React Element is the smallest building block of React apps. It is a plain JavaScript object describing what you want to see on the screen.
simpleExplanation: Imagine an architect drawing a blueprint. The blueprint is not a real house; it is just a piece of paper describing the house. A React Element is like that blueprint. It describes what a button or a div should look like, and React uses that blueprint to build the actual physical DOM element in the browser.

answers.question: What is the difference between a React Element and a Component?
answers.answer: An Element is a plain object describing what to render (e.g., `<button/>`). A Component is a function or class that RETURNS an Element (e.g., `function MyButton() { return <button/> }`).

answers.question: Are React Elements mutable?
answers.answer: No. Elements are completely immutable. Once created, you cannot change its children or attributes. The only way to update the UI is to create a brand new Element and pass it to ReactDOM.render (or update state so React does it for you).

answers.question: What is the $$typeof property used for?
answers.answer: It is a security feature. `$$typeof: Symbol.for("react.element")` ensures that an object was actually created by React and not injected by a malicious user (XSS) trying to render an arbitrary JSON object as a DOM node.
